## TL;DR

The round two review correctly found that `persistToDisk: false` was not enough: startup reachability results still entered the registry document and later unrelated saves wrote them. Startup health now lives in a volatile overlay, separate from the document. I added a regression test that sweeps health, records a route (the same unrelated-save path triggered by normal web navigation), and confirms saved health, timestamp, and `updatedAt` remain unchanged. The in-memory row and cross-server search still see the new Offline status.

I also fixed the remaining review findings: active Cmd-K searches rerun after health changes, WebKit failures only trigger health checks for connectivity errors, and attention counts are hidden while a server is not healthy. The native Hub suite passed and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed, including remote build/tests, contrast audit, and UI smoke.

The QA process did write health values into Nick's normal saved registry during both earlier review rounds. This was unintended and violated the task's isolation requirement. Review identified the round two write; the round one write had also been identified previously. I did not open or modify that external registry during this round, and there is no captured pre-QA copy in this worktree from which to restore its original health fields. The implementation now prevents startup sweeps from entering the persisted document, and the test covers an unrelated save after the sweep.

## Work and rationale

`HubAppState` now keeps startup health results in `volatileHealthByServerID`. Published entries are composed from persisted entries plus that overlay, so the sidebar, context menu, and task search see the fresh result. `document` remains the source for saves. A deliberate `refreshHealth` call with persistence enabled still updates the document; startup `refreshAllHealth` does not. Route visits, pin/edit flows, appearance changes, accent updates, and ordering continue to save the document without flushing the health overlay. Reordering explicitly retains persisted health and identity fields before saving.

The additional test extends the startup-health regression to call `recordRouteVisit` after the sweep. It asserts that the saved entry remains Healthy with its original health timestamp and edit time even though the visible entry is Offline. This exercises the later-save failure mode rather than merely checking that the startup routine itself skipped a write.

`HubCrossServerTaskSearchEngine` now retains the latest valid query. When its configured server health changes, it cancels obsolete work, updates the entries, and schedules the retained query against the new health map. Calling `cancel()` from the palette still clears the retained query, while internal cancellation used for reconfiguration does not. A test changes a configured server to Offline while a query is active and confirms the query reaches the updated offline result.

`ServerWebLoadFailure.indicatesConnectivityFailure` distinguishes offline, TLS, and timeout failures from HTTP status responses, blocked navigation, and unknown page errors. `ServerWebWorkspaceView` performs the automatic health refresh only for the first group and follows the same rule on Retry. Retry still reloads the WebView in all cases. Sidebar badges, tab badges, and the details popover now omit potentially stale attention counts unless the server is Healthy.

The earlier work also adds `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` for isolated QA registries, documents it in `macos/README.md`, displays saved server origins in sidebar rows, and corrects the auth-less serve banner to match the actual loopback bind address. Those changes remain in this branch.

## Approaches tried

Round two added a `persistToDisk` switch around the immediate store write. The review showed that this only postponed the write: the shared document was still mutated, so route history and other ordinary saves eventually flushed health fields. The correction moves startup results out of the document entirely and overlays them only for presentation. This preserves live status without making every unrelated persistence path responsible for stripping health state.

For search, deferring cancellation would leave in-flight requests using stale eligibility data. Retaining and rescheduling the active query lets the engine replace those requests using current server state. For WebKit failures, the explicit computed property makes connectivity intent testable and prevents an HTTP 404 or blocked external link from turning a reachable server Offline.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was distinguishing visible app state from the persisted registry document. The test now checks both, including after an unrelated save. The QA registry isolation mistake also means the real registry has already been modified by previous runs. No pre-run snapshot is available in this worktree, so I cannot reconstruct the former values safely; this round did not inspect or write the external file. The reviewer documented the current unwanted health stamps and states in rounds one and two.

Round two screenshots are attached in the task drawer: `.repoos/qa-screenshots/01-empty-dark.png`, `02-repoos-control-loaded.png`, `03-offline-row-before-relaunch.png`, and `04-offline-after-relaunch.png`. They were captured with `screencapture -l<windowid>` and visually inspected. They cover the initial dark shell, loaded RepoOS content, an offline row before relaunch, and the offline row after relaunch. Earlier round-one screenshots for light mode, add/edit/remove, Settings, and Cmd-K were referenced in the prior report but were not available inside this worktree during this round, so I did not attach or re-inspect them. I did not launch the Hub again in this round; the changes after round two were verified with the native test suite instead of claiming a new visual pass.

The native command was `xcodebuild -project macos/RepoOSHub.xcodeproj -scheme RepoOSHub -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath .repoos/task-1167-round3-derived CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test`; it succeeded. The scoped RepoOS check passed on the remote runner, including 123 changed-path test files (2,136 passed, 1 skipped), its additional boot timing tests, rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke test.

## Key learnings

A skipped save is not equivalent to non-persistence when mutable state shares an object graph with later saves. Volatile status must remain outside the saved document for its entire lifetime, and tests should include a subsequent ordinary write. Health-driven UI updates also need to propagate through dependent features: the search query, local-service actions, and attention badges all consume reachability state and must not remain stale when a server drops offline.
